'''Carl Theodore Bergstrom''' is a [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical]] and [[evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]] and a professor at the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle, Washington]], United States.<ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|upKiqHMAAAAJ}}</ref> Bergstrom is a critic of low-quality or misleading scientific research.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Simonite |first1=Tom |title=The Professors Who Call 'Bullshit' on Covid-19 Misinformation |url=https://www.wired.com/story/professors-call-bullshit-covid-19-misinformation/ |access-date=5 May 2020 |publisher=Wired |date=24 March 2020}}</ref> He is the co-author of a book on misinformation called ''Calling Bullshit: The Art of Skepticism in a Data-Driven World'' and teaches a class by the same name at University of Washington.<ref>{{cite web |title=Calling Bullshit |url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/563882/calling-bullshit-by-carl-t-bergstrom-and-jevin-d-west/ |website=Penguin Random House |access-date=5 May 2020}}</ref>

==Education==
Bergstrom earned his B.A. from [[Harvard University]] in 1993, then completed his [[Ph.D.]] at [[Stanford University]] under the supervision of [[Marcus Feldman]]<ref name="bergstromphd"/> in 1998.

==Research== 
Bergstrom's work concerns the flow of information through biological and social networks,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bergstrom |first1=C. T. |last2=Lachmann |first2=M. |title=The fitness value of information |journal=Oikos (Copenhagen, Denmark) |volume=119 |issue=2 |pages=219–230 |year=2006 |arxiv=q-bio.PE/0510007 |pmid=25843980 |doi=10.1111/j.1600-0706.2009.17781.x |pmc=4384894 }}</ref> as well as the ecology and evolution of [[Pathogen|pathogenic organisms]], including the development of [[Antibiotic resistance|resistance]].<ref>{{Cite journal

He is the coauthor (with [[Lee Dugatkin]]) of a college textbook, ''Evolution''.<ref name="evolbook">{{cite book |author1=Dugatkin, L. A. |author2=Bergstrom, C. T. |title=Evolution |publisher=W. W. Norton & Company |location=New York |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-393-92592-0 }}</ref> With Jevin D. West, a [[computer science]] professor at the [[University of Washington]], he developed the popular course and website "[https://callingbullshit.org/ Calling Bullshit]".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/apr/16/calling-bullshit-college-class-news-information|title='Calling bullshit': the college class on how not to be duped by the news|last=McWilliams|first=James|date=2019-04-17|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-10-08|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/science/2019/06/24/misinformation-is-everywhere-these-scientists-can-teach-you-fight-bs/|title=Misinformation is everywhere. These scientists can teach you to fight BS.|last=Guarino|first=Ben|newspaper=Washington Post|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/tech/annals-of-technology/how-to-call-bullshit-on-big-data-a-practical-guide|title=How to Call B.S. on Big Data: A Practical Guide|last=Nijhuis|first=Michele|date=2017-06-03|magazine=The New Yorker|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/helenleebouygues/2019/03/07/why-we-need-to-think-critically-about-data/|title=Why We Need To Think Critically About Data|last=Bouygues|first=Helen Lee|website=Forbes|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/how-to-call-out-bad-science-2017-2|title=This college course teaches you how to call out things that are unscientific|last=McFarling|first=Usha Lee|website=Business Insider|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/The-Fine-Art-of-Sniffing-Out/238907|title=The Fine Art of Sniffing Out Crappy Science|last=Kolowich|first=Steve|date=2017-01-16|work=The Chronicle of Higher Education|access-date=2019-10-08|language=en-US|issn=0009-5982}}</ref> His work has led to the identification of him as a resource to explain the dynamics of [[disinformation]] and misinformation,<ref>Bellware, Kim, ''[https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2020/02/10/coronavirus-is-spreading-rapidly-so-is-misinformation-about-it/ The coronavirus is spreading rapidly. So is misinformation about it.]'', The Washington Post, February 10, 2020</ref> in general. In 2025, together with Jevin West, he designed and published a free, short, online course titled “[https://thebullshitmachines.com/ Modern-Day Oracles or Bullshit Machines?]” to help understand the risk and reward of [[Large language model|large language models]], and identify misinformation generated using [[Artificial intelligence|AI technology]] <ref>{{Cite web |last=Meyers |first=Abigail |date=2025-02-26 |title=‘Modern-Day Oracles or Bullshit Machines?’: UW professors create free online course exploring the presence of AI in society |url=https://www.dailyuw.com/article/modern-day-oracles-or-bullshit-machines-uw-professors-create-free-online-course-exploring-the-presence-of-ai-in-society-20250226 |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=The Daily |language=en}}</ref>.

In addition to evolutionary biology, Bergstrom's interests include the [[Bibliometrics|ranking of scientific journals]]. In 2007, he introduced the [[Eigenfactor]],<ref name="eigenfactor"/> metrics for journal ranking.<ref>{{cite journal |first=C. T. |last=Bergstrom |date=May 2007 |title=Eigenfactor: Measuring the value and prestige of scholarly journals |journal=College & Research Libraries News |volume=68 |issue=5 |pages=314–316 |doi=10.5860/crln.68.5.7804 |doi-access=free }}</ref> This and related work on [[open access (publishing)|open access]] earned him and his father, Ted Bergstrom, the [[Scholarly Publishing and Academic Resources Coalition|SPARC Innovator Award]] in June 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sparcopen.org/our-work/innovator/bergstrom/ |title=SPARC Innovators: Ted Bergstrom and Carl Bergstrom (June 2007) |publisher=SPARC |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110828015639/http://www.arl.org/sparc/innovator/bergstroms.shtml |archive-date=2011-08-28}}</ref>
